title: Russian Drone Barrage Kills 7 in Kyiv, Including 14-Year-Old Boy; 59 Injured
detail: Russia launched sustained drone attacks on Kyiv from roughly 4:50 a.m. into the afternoon of September 25, triggering seven separate air raid alerts. A drone struck a 16-story residential building in the central Pecherskyi district between the 10th and 11th floors, killing a 14-year-old boy and injuring seven people. Further strikes hit a five-story non-residential building in the Shevchenkivskyi district (fire covering roughly 300 sq m, eight injured, the High Council of Justice building damaged), an office building and a medical facility in the Solomianskyi district, and a McDonald's warehouse in Brovary, Kyiv Oblast. By 8 p.m. local time the citywide toll stood at 7 killed (including two children) and 59 injured, with 25 people hospitalized. Mayor Vitali Klitschko confirmed the hospitalization figures; Zelensky said 'the Russians are constantly expanding their escalation operation' against civilian infrastructure and businesses. Nationwide, Russia launched 295 attack drones overnight, of which Ukrainian forces shot down or suppressed 267.

title: Ukraine Strikes Perm and Novoshakhtinsk Oil Refineries, Ulyanovsk Defense Plant, Rostov Radar Stations
detail: Ukraine's Defense Forces carried out a wave of long-range drone strikes overnight into September 25, hitting the Lukoil-Permnefteorgsintez oil refinery in Perm (~13 million tonnes/year capacity, roughly 1,500 km from the Ukrainian border) and the Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery in Rostov Oblast (~7.5 million tonnes/year), which halted operations after the strike per the regional governor. Ukrainian forces also struck the Iskra Plant defense-industry facility in Ulyanovsk, two Russian radar stations (a 64L6 Gamma-S1 and a 39N6 Kasta-2E2) in Rostov Oblast, the Efremov Synthetic Rubber Plant in Tula Oblast, and the Voronezhsintezkauchuk synthetic rubber plant in Voronezh Oblast. Zelensky said, 'We are responding to Russia's brutal strikes against life. Last night, thanks to our long-range sanctions, two oil refineries were hit — in Perm and Novoshakhtinsk,' framing the campaign as retaliation for Russia's continued strikes on Ukrainian civilians. Russia's Defense Ministry claimed it intercepted nearly 600 Ukrainian drones overnight; Moscow Times reported at least 2 killed across the industrial sites struck, unconfirmed by Ukraine.

title: Trump Makes 'Final Decision' to License Ukraine to Produce Patriot Interceptor Missiles
detail: President Zelensky announced on September 25 that President Trump has made a 'final decision' to grant Ukraine licenses to domestically produce interceptor missiles for the Patriot air defense system, telling journalists Trump had confirmed the decision during their September 22 bilateral meeting at the UN General Assembly in New York: 'Yes, I have made a final decision. Ukraine will receive licences for the production of Patriot missiles.' The move follows a reversal cycle — Trump first floated authorizing Patriot manufacturing at the July 8 NATO summit in Ankara, walked the commitment back on July 31 citing sensitivity over sharing the technology, and as recently as September 23 the US State Department told reporters no final decision had been made. The White House had not independently confirmed the announcement as of publication, and Zelensky did not specify which PAC interceptor variants would be covered or when production could begin; officials estimate domestic manufacturing capacity would take a year or more to establish. Zelensky has said Ukraine needs roughly 5% of US Patriot interceptor production to get through the winter and 10% to neutralize all Russian ballistic missile threats.

media.caption: Zelensky says Trump approved licenses for Ukraine to domestically produce Patriot interceptor missiles, September 25, 2026
